tasks.title: Tighten .ralph/instructions.md
tasks.description: Replace the single line in .ralph/instructions.md with exactly: '* Use TDD within each task — write the test, see it fail, then make it pass. Do not split a single unit of work into separate test-writing and implementation tasks.' This is defense-in-depth against future planner/task-generator subagents misreading the previous wording ('Always use TDD across all task execution') and baking TDD structure into the plan shape — which is what caused the infinite loop on task #2 in the prior run. Preserve the leading '* ' bullet marker so the markdown formatting matches the existing convention.
tasks.notes: Single-line replacement applied. The new wording explicitly forbids splitting TDD across tasks, which is the structural defense against the infinite-loop pattern from the prior run.

tasks.title: Update generate-tasks.md (both copies) with atomicity guidance
tasks.description: Add explicit 'tasks are atomic; do not split TDD across tasks' guidance to both commands/generate-tasks.md and .claude/commands/generate-tasks.md. The two files are mirrors (ralph init copies commands/*.md into each project's .claude/commands/). Keep them in sync — edit both identically. Add a new rule under the task-structure section stating: each task is one atomic unit of work; do not create paired 'write tests for X' / 'implement X' tasks; if TDD is desired, the executor agent practices it within the task (write test, see it fail, make it pass, all in one task). After editing, run `diff commands/generate-tasks.md .claude/commands/generate-tasks.md` to confirm they are identical.

tasks.title: Update review-tasks.md (both copies) to flag paired test/impl
tasks.description: Update commands/review-tasks.md and .claude/commands/review-tasks.md (mirrors — keep in sync). Under the Atomicity check section, add: paired test/impl tasks against the same files are a FAIL finding — each task must be a complete atomic unit. The reviewer subagent should flag and reject any plan that splits work this way. After editing, run `diff commands/review-tasks.md .claude/commands/review-tasks.md` to confirm identical.

tasks.title: Implement readTasksFile + writeTasksFile + snapshotTasksFile + corruption.log
tasks.description: The stub at src/tasks-file.ts currently exports TasksFile interface, TasksFileError class, and three throwing stubs (readTasksFile/writeTasksFile/snapshotTasksFile). The failing test suite already exists at test/tasks-file.test.ts (10 tests) with fixtures under test/fixtures/ (tasks-valid.json, tasks-missing-comma.json, tasks-unescaped-quote.json, tasks-trailing-garbage.json) — this was work product from a prior (incorrectly-split) task; reuse it as-is. Step 1: confirm the tests currently fail against the stubs (that's the TDD red). Step 2: implement the three functions. (a) readTasksFile(path, opts?: { dataDir?: string }) → { data: TasksFile, repaired: boolean, restored: boolean, error?: string } — try JSON.parse first; on failure try jsonrepair (already installed via prior task, imports as `import { jsonrepair } from 'jsonrepair'`) returning { data, repaired: true }; on still-failure read <dataDir>/.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json and parse it, returning { data, restored: true }; if all three paths fail throw TasksFileError with a descriptive message. Every failure path (parse fail, jsonrepair fail, snapshot fail) must appendFileSync a JSONL entry to <dataDir>/corruption.log with { ts: ISO8601, stage: 'parse'|'jsonrepair'|'snapshot', error: string, sha256: hex(sha256(bytes)), preview: bytes.slice(0,500).toString('utf-8') }. Use crypto.createHash('sha256') for the sha256. (b) writeTasksFile(path, data) — JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) to <path>.tmp then fs.renameSync to <path> for atomic semantics. (c) snapshotTasksFile(path, dataDir) — copy the current tasks.json to <dataDir>/.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json (single overwriting file, not rotated). Do NOT implement mutateTasksFile here — that is task 6. Make all 10 existing tests pass without regressing other tests.

tasks.title: Implement mutateTasksFile with atomicity tests
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/tasks-file.test.ts with failing tests for a new mutateTasksFile(path: string, fn: (data: TasksFile) => void | TasksFile, opts?: { dataDir?: string }) helper. Tests must cover: (a) tempfile <path>.tmp is written BEFORE rename — spy on fs.writeFileSync and fs.renameSync to verify ordering; (b) rename happens on successful fn; (c) tempfile is cleaned up (via fs.unlinkSync) when fn throws AND the original tasks.json is left untouched; (d) unknown/extra fields on task objects are preserved across the round-trip (e.g., a 'customField' on a task survives); (e) after successful mutation and when opts.dataDir is provided, snapshotTasksFile has been called (spy on it). Step 2: implement mutateTasksFile in src/tasks-file.ts: call readTasksFile(path, opts); call fn(data) — support both in-place mutation AND returning a new object; call writeTasksFile(path, result); call snapshotTasksFile(path, opts.dataDir) when opts.dataDir is provided. Use try/finally to ensure tempfile cleanup on throw. Preserve unknown fields by round-tripping the raw parsed object (don't project into a narrower type). Make new tests pass without regressing task 5's tests.

tasks.title: Implement ralph task subcommand group + wire into index.ts
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: create test/commands/task.test.ts with failing tests covering every subcommand: (1) 'task start <id> --iteration N' sets status to 'in-progress' and is idempotent on re-run; (2) 'task complete <id> --iteration N --notes "..."' sets status:'complete', completedAt to fresh ISO 8601, completedBy to 'iteration-N', and notes to the provided string; (3) 'task complete <id> --iteration N --notes-file PATH' reads notes from the file; (4) 'task complete <id> --iteration N --notes-file -' reads notes from stdin; (5) 'task complete <id> --iteration N' with no notes flag leaves notes untouched; (6) 'task note <id> "x"' appends via ' | ' separator (matching src/test-validator.ts appendNote semantics); 'task note <id> --replace "x"' overwrites; (7) 'task set-status <id> <status>' accepts only pending|in-progress|complete|blocked and rejects others with non-zero exit; (8) 'task add --file PATH' validates the payload against src/tasks-schema.json via ajv and REFUSES on validation failure with exit code 1 and stderr 'ralph task add: validation failed — <field>: <reason>'; on success the new task is appended to tasks.tasks[]; (9) 'task show <id>' prints formatted JSON, read-only (does not call writeTasksFile). Use a tmp tasks.json per test to isolate. Step 2: run 'bun add ajv' to install the validator. Step 3: implement src/commands/task.ts using Commander subcommands (mirror the style of src/commands/run.ts and src/commands/plan.ts). Every mutating subcommand goes through mutateTasksFile from src/tasks-file.ts. Refuse-to-merge contract for 'add': exit 1, print to stderr 'ralph task add: validation failed — <field>: <reason>', leave tasks.json untouched. Step 4: wire the command group into src/index.ts Commander dispatch alongside the other subcommands. Step 5: run 'bun run build' at the end to confirm the binary still compiles.

tasks.title: Rewrite buildSystemPrompt() to use ralph task CLI
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/commands/run.test.ts with failing assertions against buildSystemPrompt(). Assert the rendered prompt CONTAINS: 'ralph task start' with an iteration placeholder pattern; 'ralph task complete' with '--iteration' and '--notes-file'; the notes-tempfile path pattern '<dataDir>/.ralph_task_<id>_notes.md' (use the resolved dataDir from the test harness); 'ralph task add --file' in the DISCOVER-AND-DOCUMENT block; and an explicit ban substring like 'Do NOT use Edit or Write on' paired with 'tasks.json'. Also assert the prompt does NOT contain 'Use Edit to set these fields' (old phrasing). Keep existing assertions intact. Confirm tests fail against the current implementation. Step 2: update buildSystemPrompt() in src/commands/run.ts. Replace step 1 ('set status to in-progress') with: 'Run: ralph task start <id> --iteration <N>' where N is input.iteration. Replace step 5 (the 'Use Edit to set these fields' block) with: (a) 'Write your completion notes to <dataDir>/.ralph_task_<id>_notes.md using the Write tool' — supply the absolute path; (b) 'Run: ralph task complete <id> --iteration <N> --notes-file <dataDir>/.ralph_task_<id>_notes.md'. Add an explicit ban near the CRITICAL RULES block: 'Do NOT use Edit or Write on .ralph/tasks.json directly — the ralph task subcommands are the only supported path.' Update the DISCOVER-AND-DOCUMENT block: replace the 'add them as new pending tasks in tasks.json' line with 'Use ralph task add --file <path> to append a new task (the CLI validates the payload before merging).' Keep all other prompt structure unchanged.

tasks.title: Migrate test-validator.ts to defensive I/O
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/test-validator.test.ts with failing tests: (a) malformed tasks.json (missing comma) is recovered via readTasksFile; validateTaskTests runs the test command and still writes back via writeTasksFile; (b) when readTasksFile throws TasksFileError (both parse AND snapshot fail), validateTaskTests returns { status: 'error', message } rather than crashing — preserve the existing ValidationResult return-shape contract; (c) snapshotTasksFile is called after each write (spy on it). Step 2: migrate src/test-validator.ts. Replace the bare 'JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))' at line ~70 with readTasksFile from src/tasks-file.ts; replace the writeFileSync calls (at lines ~86, ~93, ~102 — three timeout/can't-run/revert paths) with writeTasksFile plus snapshotTasksFile. Preserve the appendNote semantics exactly (append with ' | ' separator). Do NOT change the ValidationResult enum or the CANT_RUN_PATTERNS list. Make new tests pass without regressing existing validator tests.

tasks.title: Migrate task-archiver.ts + stop silent swallowing
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/task-archiver.test.ts with failing tests: (a) archiver uses readTasksFile so corrupted tasks.json can be repaired and archival proceeds normally; (b) when readTasksFile throws TasksFileError, the archiver returns { archivedCount: 0, prevNotes: null, warnings: [<string>] } AND appends an entry to <dataDir>/corruption.log AND appends a line to the iteration log (pass iterationLogPath into archiveCompletedTasks opts if not already present). Current behavior silently swallows parse errors (src/task-archiver.ts:27-31) — the new test must catch that and require it be surfaced. Step 2: migrate src/task-archiver.ts. Add a 'warnings: string[]' field to the ArchiveResult type. Replace the try/catch at lines 27-31 with a readTasksFile call; on TasksFileError, push a descriptive message to warnings AND log to the iteration log (and corruption.log is already written by readTasksFile); replace every JSON.stringify+writeFileSync pair with writeTasksFile + snapshotTasksFile. Document in task notes the choice of warnings[] over an onError callback (simpler test harness, easier to assert on). Make new tests pass without regressing existing archiver tests.

tasks.title: Migrate run.ts reads + snapshot + corruption counter + tempfile cleanup
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/commands/run.test.ts with failing tests covering: (a) main-loop read at src/commands/run.ts:445 goes through readTasksFile; (b) post-task-review status re-read at src/commands/run.ts:571 goes through readTasksFile; (c) a corruptionEvents counter initialised to 0 increments by 1 whenever readTasksFile returns repaired:true or restored:true anywhere it's called in runRun; (d) the final summary (src/commands/run.ts:610-619 block) emits a new line exactly '⚠ N corruption events recovered this run — see <dataDir>/corruption.log' ONLY when N > 0; when N === 0 the line is absent; (e) the ntfy notification body includes the corruption count when config.narration.ntfyTopic is set; (f) after the main-loop read succeeds, snapshotTasksFile is called (per-iteration snapshot); (g) the TEMP_FILES cleanup at src/commands/run.ts:345 is extended to glob-sweep files matching .ralph_task_<id>_notes.md under dataDir at run end — use fs.readdirSync(dataDir).filter(f => /^\.ralph_task_\d+_notes\.md$/.test(f)) rather than importing a glob library. Step 2: implement all seven in src/commands/run.ts. Make all new tests pass without regressing existing run tests.

tasks.title: Tighten post-task-reviewer path-scoped allowlist
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: add a failing assertion to test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts using the existing mock-spawn pattern. Find the test that captures the args array passed to spawn by spawnPostTaskReviewer. Add an assertion that the args array contains '--allowedTools' immediately followed by the EXACT string 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit(.ralph/review-post.md),Write(.ralph/review-post.md)'. The current production value at src/post-task-reviewer.ts:124 is 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write' — confirm the test fails against the current value (that's the TDD verification). Step 2: change the --allowedTools value in src/post-task-reviewer.ts:119-129 from 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write' to 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit(.ralph/review-post.md),Write(.ralph/review-post.md)'. This activates Claude Code's path-scoped allowlist enforcement (verified April 2026 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md): Edit and Write outside .ralph/review-post.md will be denied before hitting disk. No other changes to the file. Make the new test pass without regressing any other post-task-reviewer tests.

tasks.title: Tighten post-task-reviewer prompt (belt-and-suspenders)
tasks.description: Add an explicit rule near the top of agents/post-task-reviewer.md: a new line stating 'You may only write to .ralph/review-post.md — never modify .ralph/tasks.json.' This is defense-in-depth alongside the path-scoped allowlist from task 12 (the allowlist is the authoritative enforcement; the prompt keeps the agent from even trying). Preserve the existing '## Output Format' and '## Coverage Diagram' sections verbatim — do not reword or restructure them. Smoke-read the file after editing to confirm it still reads as a coherent agent prompt (no orphaned fragments, no broken section headers).

tasks.title: Document ralph task workflow in CLAUDE.md
tasks.description: Add a short 4-6 line section to CLAUDE.md under the 'Conventions' section (or a new 'Agent workflow' subsection if cleaner) explaining: agents must use the ralph task subcommand group (start, complete, note, set-status, add, show) for every mutation of .ralph/tasks.json; direct Edit/Write on .ralph/tasks.json is forbidden and is caught by the per-agent prompt ban plus the path-scoped allowlist on the post-task reviewer; the CLI ensures atomic writes and JSON validity so corruption becomes structurally impossible via this path. Keep the addition tight — do not rewrite the existing 'Architecture' or 'Key design patterns' sections; only add the new guidance.

tasks.title: Full-suite verification + build + manual corruption-recovery smoke test
tasks.description: Final verification task. Step 1: run 'bun test' — full suite must pass green. Step 2: run 'bun run build' — must produce a fresh dist/ralph without errors. Step 3: manual checks on a scratch project (create a throwaway dir with a hand-written tasks.json): (3a) run 'ralph task start 1 --iteration 1' then 'ralph task complete 1 --iteration 1 --notes "manual smoke"' then 'ralph task note 1 "appended"' then 'ralph task note 1 --replace "replaced"' — after each command, cat tasks.json and verify it parses as valid JSON. (3b) Deliberately break tasks.json (delete a comma after a notes field in any task); run 'ralph run' on the scratch project for one iteration; verify readTasksFile recovered via jsonrepair (look for the success path continuing) and that <dataDir>/corruption.log contains a new entry with stage:'jsonrepair'. (3c) Delete BOTH tasks.json AND .ralph/.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json; run 'ralph run' — verify TasksFileError is surfaced (not a silent failure) and the corruption.log entry records the complete fail. (3d) In a separate scratch repo with review.postTask enabled, trigger a post-task review and verify the reviewer cannot Edit .ralph/tasks.json — the Edit call should be denied by Claude Code's path-scoped allowlist; confirm by reading the stream-json output for a permission_denied event. Record all four results in the task's notes on completion. If any step fails, leave the task in-progress and document the failure in notes for the next iteration.
